@graph.name: Is VOS a NECS Entree alternative, and is it better than NECS Entree?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither question quite fits, and we would rather lead with that. Entree is the software your company runs on, and VOS handles how an order gets in. At getting an order out of a kitchen that will not use an order form, VOS is the better answer. At everything else Entree does the question does not apply: we have no ledger, no payables, no warehouse module and no proof of delivery, and no plan to build any of them. Compare them as like for like and one of the two will disappoint you badly.

@graph.name: Does Entree not already have customer ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: It does, and anyone telling you otherwise has not looked. They offer web order entry and mobile order entry, plus a rep order pad. All of it works by a person finding items and typing quantities. The accounts who were never going to do that are the ones this is for.

@graph.name: Will this touch our installation or our version?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nobody signs into your distribution software to set this up. We work from an export of your item lists, and the order comes back to you as a file or a feed. Your version, your upgrade schedule and your support arrangement are all unaffected.

@graph.name: We are thinking of moving off Entree. Can you help?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not with the migration itself, no. Replacing it means replacing accounting, ledger, payables, EDI and warehouse functions together, and that is an ERP selection rather than an ordering decision. VOS can run before or after such a project, and orders can keep arriving as a file while the rest moves.

They are not comparable, and a quote for one tells you nothing about the other. Neither of us publishes figures. Ours is quoted for your own book, and it is a far narrower decision than choosing the system your whole company runs on.

@graph.name: How fast could this be live?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors this goes live inside 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens get a first order in that day. There is no project here because there is nothing to integrate into, which is the main reason a NECS Entree alternative gets looked at without anybody intending to replace anything.

@graph.name: And the accounts that will only ever call?

acceptedAnswer.text: They carry on calling, and your desk deals with those the way it always has. Be clear about the limit though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number from VOS, no timestamp and nothing moving in stock. Only what comes through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the Entree details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Read off necs.com on 10 October 2026: the module list, the 1987 founding date, the Windows description and the web, mobile and rep ordering products. They publish no price and no implementation process, so this page guesses at neither. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.
